einzeiler: Steve Jobs' wilderness years between Apple and his triumphant return.
kurzfassung: After being ousted from Apple following the Macintosh crisis, Steve Jobs spent over a decade in the wilderness founding NeXT and funding Pixar. During this transformative period, he burned through millions on impractical hardware designs and alienated investors before finally learning crucial lessons in leadership and pragmatism. His eventual return to Apple, driven by the acquisition of NeXT's superior software, laid the groundwork for the company's modern renaissance.
stichpunkte: Steve Jobs was pushed out of Apple in 1985 after a failed coup attempt against CEO John Sculley and weak Macintosh sales.
He founded NeXT Computer, aiming to build high-end machines for scientists and universities using an integrated hardware and software approach.
NeXT suffered from extreme financial strain due to Jobs' perfectionism, such as insisting on a flawless manufacturing cube and spending heavily on a Paul Rand logo.
Jobs alienated key partners, famously backing out of massive government contracts that Ross Perot had lined up.
Despite hardware failures, NeXT developed revolutionary object-oriented software that would later form the foundation of Apple's modern operating systems.
Simultaneously, Jobs personally funded Pixar, achieving massive financial freedom and an eventual billionaire status when Pixar went public after Toy Story.
Apple, facing bankruptcy and a failing operating system in the late 1990s, acquired NeXT and brought Jobs back into the fold.
Upon returning as interim CEO, Jobs ruthlessly streamlined Apple's product lines by 70 percent and later brokered a crucial bailout deal with Microsoft.

beschreibung:
We all know the Steve Jobs who came back in the late 1990s and saved Apple from becoming a footnote. And we've all heard the story of how, in 1985, he was pushed out of the company he'd created.

What we don't know is what happened in between.

Geoffrey Cain spent years reconstructing the decade Jobs spent outside Apple. NeXT spent years losing money. His co-founders left. His investors lost faith. His fortune nearly disappeared. At one point, he was a weekend away from shutting the company down.

Somewhere in those failures, Jobs learned how to become the leader Apple would eventually need.

This is Steve Jobs before he became Steve Jobs.
